{{Short description|Norwegian chemist (1929–2022)}}
'''Peter Klæboe''' (17 November 1929 – 27 February 2022) was a [[Norway|Norwegian]] chemist.

He took the [[cand.real.]] degree at the [[University of Oslo]] in 1956, the PhD degree at the [[University of Oklahoma]] in 1960 and the [[dr.philos.]] degree in Oslo in 1967. Upon returning from the US in 1960 he was hired as lecturer at the University of Oslo, advancing to [[docent]] and then professor of [[physical chemistry]]. His pioneering field was [[molecular spectroscopy]]. Retiring as a professor in 1999, he continued his research nonetheless and had by his 80th birthday penned 350 scientific articles. He was a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] and the [[Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters]].<ref name=ntb>{{cite news|title=80 år 17. november: Professor Peter Klæboe|agency=Norwegian News Agency|date=30 October 2009|language=Norwegian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Dagens navn|date=17 November 1989|work=Aftenposten|language=Norwegian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Peter Klæboe|date=28 March 2022|work=Aftenposten|language=no|page=53}}</ref>

Klæboe died on 27 February 2022.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Trygve Helgaker |author2=Claus J. Nielsen |author3=Einar Uggerud |title=Peter Klæboe var en sann gentleman |url=https://www.aftenposten.no/nekrolog/i/9Kdxop/peter-klaeboe-var-en-sann-gentleman |website=Aftenposten |access-date=19 December 2022 |date=27 March 2022}}</ref>
